text.p: The popularity of France's new leftist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has dipped but most voters remain confident he can solve France's problems, an opinion poll showed on Thursday.

The Sofres survey for the weekly Le Figaro magazine showed that 62 percent of French people trusted Jospin to solve the nation's woes while 35 percent lacked confidence in him. A month ago, his rating was 66-31.
Voter confidence in conservative President Jacques Chirac edged up one point to 47 percent, but 51 percent were still sceptical about his ability to tackle France's problems.

Chirac has gained nine percentage points in the Sofres poll since he dissolved the National Assembly in April and called early legislative elections in a disastrous bid to get his centre-right allies re-elected.
An alliance of Socialists, Communists and Greens scored an upset victory in the June 1 second round.

The poll was carried out on July 23-25, giving voters a chance to react to the new government's first measures, including new corporate taxes to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999.
